item.title: [PBV7-487] Automate Redis and Kubernetes infrastructure with Helm
item.description:
Source and parent

Specification: Realtime WebSocket Platform – .NET 10, Redis, and Kubernetes
Parent Epic: PBV7-484

Context

Package the gateway and Redis infrastructure so a new environment can be created repeatably while also supporting an existing external Redis service. Infrastructure automation must be safe to rerun and must comply with the governing Propago scripting standard.

Requirements

  • Create and version the realtime-gateway Helm chart.
  • Support an external Redis endpoint through existing Kubernetes secrets and configuration.
  • Provide an optional dedicated Redis deployment using an approved, pinned Helm chart and environment-specific values.
  • Define Redis authentication, ACLs, TLS decision, persistence, replication/failover, topology, anti-affinity, PodDisruptionBudget, resource limits, metrics, backup, and restore behavior.
  • Separate session and realtime users, credentials, prefixes, and connection configuration.
  • Add Kubernetes Deployment, ClusterIP Service, ConfigMaps, Secrets references, startup/readiness/liveness probes, security context, service account, PodDisruptionBudget, topology spread, resource requests/limits, NetworkPolicy, and autoscaling inputs.
  • Use Propago <environment>-<application> naming.
  • Create PowerShell 7 automation for prerequisite validation, Redis installation or external validation, gateway installation, upgrade, validation, rollback, and explicitly guarded teardown.
  • Resolve the current scripting standard from PropagoLLC/Standards; current baseline is Scripts version 4.0.
  • Validate PowerShell, .NET, Git, container CLI, Helm, kubectl, Kubernetes context, cluster, namespace, permissions, chart versions, secrets, DNS, and network reachability before changes.
  • Implement idempotent CREATED, UPDATED, UNCHANGED, and SKIPPED behavior.
  • Evaluate concurrency; serialize shared Helm/Kubernetes mutations and use bounded locking so simultaneous runs cannot corrupt a release.
  • Back up or capture existing Helm values and Kubernetes resources before meaningful changes.
  • Provide dry-run/diff behavior, bounded waits, rollback, final validation, meaningful exit codes, summary output, and secret-redacted logs.
  • Apply standard log housekeeping: retain seven days uncompressed, archive older completed logs to validated ZIP files, and preserve originals if archive validation fails.
  • Include a package README covering requirements, files, parameters, execution, output, rollback, limitations, and troubleshooting.

Dependencies

  • Standalone gateway container.
  • Kubernetes target environments and namespace strategy.
  • Approved Redis chart/version or external endpoint.
  • Storage class, secret-management, backup, and metrics decisions.

Completion criteria

  • A blank approved namespace can receive a complete gateway deployment through the documented automation.
  • External Redis and Helm-managed Redis modes are both supported and mutually explicit.
  • Repeated execution converges without duplicate or unnecessary changes.
  • Helm artifacts are versioned, configurable, and contain no embedded credentials.
  • Destructive actions require explicit targeting and force/confirmation controls.
  • Rollback restores the previous healthy application release and configuration.
  • All PowerShell files pass complete parser validation and Scripts standard 4.0 validation.

Testing criteria

  • Run helm lint, rendered-template validation, Kubernetes schema checks, context confirmation, kubectl diff, and server-side dry-run.
  • Test clean install, unchanged rerun, configuration update, application upgrade, failed rollout, and rollback.
  • Test missing CLI, unsupported version, wrong context, wrong namespace, missing secret, invalid values, unreachable cluster, and insufficient permissions.
  • Test concurrent invocation and verify bounded lock acquisition, useful timeout behavior, and no partial conflicting release.
  • Test Redis persistence, replica/failover behavior, backup, restore, authentication, ACL isolation, and metrics.
  • Verify NetworkPolicy permits only required ingress and egress.
  • Verify health checks, rollout status, final application-level validation, logs, archives, summaries, and exit codes.
  • Verify credentials are absent from source, rendered output, command-line arguments, logs, reports, and exception text.
